b1-06.explain: When you hope, want, doubt or judge something about someone else's action, use que + present subjunctive: espero que lo haga, quiere que la llames, es importante que no se haga ilusiones, no creo que conteste. The subjunctive marks the action as wished or uncertain, not a fact. English often uses an infinitive ('she wants you to call'). Watch out: creo que (belief) takes the indicative: Creo que contestará. With one subject, use the infinitive: espero volver.
examples: No creo que ella conteste pronto.
I don't think she'll answer soon.
Es importante que no se haga ilusiones antes de tiempo.
It's important that she doesn't get her hopes up too early.
Rocío quiere que la llames.
Rocío wants you to call her.
Creo que contestará pronto.
I think she'll answer soon.

b1-06.explain: Negative tú commands are no + the tú form of the present subjunctive, the same forms you see after espero que: no vendas, no te rías, no le digas. -ar verbs switch to -es, -er/-ir verbs to -as, and irregulars keep the yo stem (digo → no digas). Pronouns go before the verb; in affirmative commands they are attached: dile / no le digas. Watch out: *no vende and *no le dices are typical learner mistakes.
examples: No te rías de mí.
Don't laugh at me.
Todavía no, no le digas nada.
Not yet, don't tell her anything.
Y tú, mija, no vendas la casa todavía.
And you, dear, don't sell the house yet.
Dile que por fin puede afinar la guitarra.
Tell him he can finally tune that guitar.

b1-06.explain: Two very common verb + de + infinitive phrases. Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something': Mi padre acaba de ver esta foto = My father has just seen this photo. In the present (acaba de) it describes something that happened a moment ago. Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something': dejé de preguntar = I stopped asking; no ha dejado de llorar = he hasn't stopped crying. Terminar de + infinitive works the same way and means 'to finish doing': cuando termines de leerlas. Watch out: the de is never dropped, and the verb after it is always an infinitive: *acaba ver and *dejé preguntar are wrong.
examples: Mi padre acaba de ver esta foto y no ha dejado de llorar.
My father has just seen this photo and hasn't stopped crying.
Por orgullo dejé de preguntar por él.
Out of pride I stopped asking about him.
Cuando termines de leerlas —dijo Marisol—, Rocío quiere que la llames.
"When you finish reading them," said Marisol, "Rocío wants you to call her."

b1-09.explain: To report an order, use decir, pedir or gritar + que + subjunctive. After a past verb, use the imperfect subjunctive: «No usen el ascensor» → gritaba que no usaran el ascensor. After a present verb, the present subjunctive: dice que no usemos el ascensor. Decir que + indicative only reports information: decía que la oscuridad le daba miedo. Watch out: 'told him not to be afraid' is le dijo que no tuviera miedo, never *le dijo no tener miedo.
examples: Abajo, en el vestíbulo, la portera, doña Rosa, gritaba que no usaran el ascensor y que bajaran con cuidado por las escaleras.
Downstairs, in the lobby, the doorwoman, doña Rosa, was shouting for people not to use the elevator and to come down the stairs carefully.
Soledad se arrodilló a su lado, le dijo que no tuviera miedo y le propuso un juego para distraerlo.
Soledad knelt beside him, told him not to be afraid and suggested a game to distract him.
«Traigan velas.» → Doña Rosa nos pidió que trajéramos velas.
"Bring candles." → Doña Rosa asked us to bring candles.

b1-09.topic: Verbs of change: ponerse, quedarse, convertirse
b1-09.explain: English 'get / become / turn' has several equivalents. Ponerse + adjective: a quick change of colour, mood or appearance (se puso negro, se puso nervioso). Quedarse + adjective or participle: the state left after something happens (se quedó dormido, se quedó callado). Convertirse en + noun: a real transformation (se convirtió en una cocina). Volverse and hacerse follow at B2. Watch out: convertirse needs en + a noun, so *el cielo se convirtió negro is wrong.
examples: Aquella tarde de octubre, sin embargo, el cielo se puso negro y una tormenta enorme empezó a golpear las ventanas.
That October afternoon, however, the sky turned black and an enormous storm began to pound the windows.
Durante la siguiente hora, el edificio entero se convirtió en una cocina improvisada.
During the following hour, the whole building turned into an improvised kitchen.
Gonzalo se quedó dormido sobre las piernas de su madre, con una sonrisa tranquila.
Gonzalo fell asleep on his mother's lap, with a peaceful smile.
Cuando se fue la luz, Soledad se puso furiosa y el señor mayor se quedó callado.
When the power went out, Soledad got furious and the old man went quiet.

b1-09.topic: Accidental se: se le olvidó, se le acabó
b1-09.explain: To talk about accidents and things that happen without anyone meaning them, Spanish uses se + an indirect object pronoun (me, te, le, nos, les) + the verb: se le olvidó guardar, se le acabó la batería, se me va a descongelar. The thing that is forgotten, runs out or defrosts is the subject, so the verb agrees with it: se le acabó la batería, se le acabaron las velas. The pronoun shows who it happened to. Compare olvidé el archivo (neutral) with se me olvidó el archivo ('it slipped my mind', it wasn't on purpose). Watch out: the order is always se + pronoun + verb: se le olvidó, never *le se olvidó.
examples: A su computadora se le estaba acabando la batería.
Her computer's battery was running out.
Se le había olvidado guardar el archivo.
She had forgotten to save the file.
Se me va a descongelar el congelador y no pienso desperdiciar tanta comida.
My freezer is going to defrost on me and I'm not going to waste so much food.

b1-10.explain: Se + a third-person verb says what is done when the doer doesn't matter. The verb agrees with the thing: se pone el molde, las alfombras se hacen. With no noun, se means 'you / people'. English uses 'is made' or 'you put'. In b1-04 you met se puede; here se carries a subject. Not every se is passive: se rio and se cae describe the subject. Watch out: plural thing, plural verb: se ven muchas puertas, not *se ve.
examples: Se pone sobre el aserrín y se llena de colores.
You put it on the sawdust and fill it with colors.
Las alfombras no se hacen para durar.
Carpets aren't made to last.
A la derecha se veía la mitad de una puerta.
On the right you could see half of a door.
En Antigua se venden tejidos en muchas tiendas.
Woven textiles are sold in lots of shops in Antigua.

b1-10.explain: This returns here from b1-05. Para points forward to a goal: purpose (para tocar, para durar) and, with a new subject, para que + subjunctive (para que las monjas pudieran cruzar). Por points back to a cause or along a path: por eso ('that's why'), por esa calle, and fixed phrases like por primera vez. Watch out: English 'for/to' hides the difference: 'made to last' is para durar; para eso means 'for that purpose', not 'that's why'.
examples: Por eso la llamamos Antigua.
That's why we call it Antigua.
Si caminamos por esa calle, encontraremos la casa.
If we walk along that street, we'll find the house.
Lo construyeron en el siglo XVII para que las monjas pudieran cruzar la calle sin ser vistas.
They built it in the seventeenth century so the nuns could cross the street without being seen.
En Antigua muchas puertas tienen una aldaba con forma de mano, para tocar.
In Antigua many doors have a door knocker shaped like a hand, for knocking.

b1-10.explain: The future tense can also express a guess about the present. ¿Qué será? means 'What can it be? / I wonder what it is', and ¿Quién vivirá aquí ahora? means 'I wonder who lives here now'. Nothing is in the future: the speaker is wondering or guessing. In a statement it means 'probably': Será la casa = It's probably the house. The forms are the normal future (ser → será, vivir → vivirá). Watch out: this story also uses the future with its real meaning (esta noche verás la lava, encontraremos la casa, iré contigo). A question or guess about now is probability; a plan or prediction is the real future.
examples: ¿Y qué será «la mano que toca»?
And what can 'the hand that knocks' be?
¿Será alguien que toca la guitarra?
Could it be someone who plays the guitar?
¿Quién vivirá aquí ahora?
Who could be living here now?

b1-06.q: Ximena hopes the daughter will write back. Complete: Espero que la hija de Octavio me ___ pronto.
b1-06.why: Espero que + a different subject takes the present subjunctive: (ella) conteste. Contesta is indicative, the infinitive needs the same subject, and contestes is the tú form.

b1-06.q: Complete: Creo que la abuela ___ feliz con las cartas, pero no creo que ___ dormir esta noche.
b1-06.why: Creo que states a belief, so indicative (estará). No creo que expresses doubt, so subjunctive (pueda).

b1-06.q: Marisol tells her cousin (tú): 'Don't tell her anything.'
b1-06.why: Negative tú command = no + present subjunctive: digas (from digo). Pronoun before the verb. No le dices is a statement; dile is only affirmative.

b1-06.q: Rocío's father saw the photo a few minutes ago. Complete: «Mi padre ___ ver esta foto.»
b1-06.why: Acabar de + infinitive means 'to have just done something': acaba de ver = has just seen. The de can't be dropped, and deja de means 'stops'.

options: Es importante que no se hace ilusiones.
b1-06.why: Es importante que is a value judgement and needs the subjunctive: se haga. Creo que (belief) correctly takes the indicative.

b1-06.q: Make the command negative: «Dile la verdad.» → «___ la verdad.»
b1-06.why: In a negative command the pronoun moves in front and the verb becomes subjunctive: dile → no le digas.

b1-06.q: What does «Por orgullo dejé de preguntar por él» mean?
options: Out of pride I kept asking about him.
Out of pride I stopped asking about him.
Out of pride I let him ask about me.
Out of pride I had just asked about him.
b1-06.why: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something': dejé de preguntar = I stopped asking. 'Had just asked' would be acababa de preguntar.

b1-06.q: Which sentence correctly says 'Marisol hopes to find more letters'?
options: Marisol espera que encuentra más cartas.
Marisol espera que encuentre más cartas.
Marisol espera a encontrar más cartas.
b1-06.why: Same subject (Marisol hopes, Marisol finds) → infinitive. Que + subjunctive means someone else will find them.

b1-09.q: Doña Rosa gritaba: «¡No usen el ascensor!» Complete the report: Doña Rosa gritaba que no ___ el ascensor.
b1-09.why: A reported command after a past verb (gritaba) needs que + imperfect subjunctive: usaran. Usaban would report a fact, not an order.

b1-09.q: Complete: Doña Rosa nos pide que ___ con cuidado por las escaleras.
b1-09.why: Pedir que + subjunctive. The reporting verb is present (pide), so the present subjunctive follows: bajemos. Que can't be followed by an infinitive.

b1-09.topic: Accidental se: se le olvidó, se le acabó
b1-09.q: Soledad didn't mean to forget. Complete: «Se le ___ guardar el archivo.»
b1-09.why: In accidental se the verb agrees with what is forgotten. An infinitive (guardar el archivo) counts as singular, so se le olvidó. Le shows who it happened to.

b1-09.topic: Verbs of change: ponerse, quedarse, convertirse
b1-09.q: Complete: Después de cenar, Gonzalo se ___ dormido sobre las piernas de su madre.
b1-09.why: Quedarse + participle or adjective describes the state that results: quedarse dormido = fall asleep. Ponerse and volverse don't go with dormido; convertirse needs en + noun.

b1-09.q: In which sentence does the verb report an order, not a piece of information?
options: Gonzalo decía que la oscuridad le daba miedo.
Gutiérrez contó que su esposa había fallecido.
La compañía eléctrica dice que el apagón puede durar toda la noche.
Soledad le dijo que no tuviera miedo.
b1-09.why: Decir que + subjunctive (tuviera) reports a command: 'told him not to be afraid'. With the indicative (daba, había fallecido, puede) it only reports information.

b1-09.topic: Accidental se: se le olvidó, se le acabó
b1-09.q: The computer's battery ran out. Which sentence is correct?
options: A la computadora le se acabó la batería.
A la computadora se le acabaron la batería.
A la computadora se le acabó la batería.
La computadora se acabó la batería.
b1-09.why: The order is se + le + verb, and the verb agrees with la batería (singular): se le acabó. Le se is never correct.

b1-09.topic: Verbs of change: ponerse, quedarse, convertirse
options: El cielo se puso negro y el vestíbulo se convirtió en un comedor.
El cielo se puso negro y el vestíbulo se convirtió un comedor.
El cielo se convirtió negro y el vestíbulo se puso un comedor.
El cielo se puso en negro y el vestíbulo se quedó un comedor.
b1-09.why: Ponerse + adjective for a sudden change (se puso negro); convertirse en + noun for a transformation. Without en, convertirse is wrong.

b1-09.topic: Accidental se: se le olvidó, se le acabó
b1-09.q: What does «Se me va a descongelar el congelador» tell us about Gutiérrez?
options: He wants to defrost the freezer on purpose.
The freezer is going to defrost and it isn't his fault.
He has already defrosted the freezer.
Someone else is going to defrost his freezer.
b1-09.why: Se me + verb presents something as an accident that happens to the speaker: the blackout, not Gutiérrez, is defrosting the freezer.

b1-10.q: Complete: En Antigua, las alfombras de Viernes Santo se ___ con aserrín de colores.
b1-10.why: Passive se agrees with the thing: las alfombras is plural, so se hacen. Se hace is the classic slip; hecho needs ser or estar.

b1-10.q: Itzel is wondering about the clue. Complete her question: ¿Y qué ___ «la mano que toca»?
b1-10.why: To wonder or guess about the present, Spanish uses the future: ¿qué será? = what can it be? Sea and fuera are subjunctive forms with no trigger, and seré is the yo form.

b1-10.q: Complete: Bayron e Itzel caminaron ___ la calle del arco ___ buscar la casa.
b1-10.why: Por marks the path (along the street); para + infinitive marks the purpose (in order to look for).

b1-10.q: Complete: Construyeron el arco ___ que las monjas pudieran cruzar la calle sin ser vistas.
b1-10.why: Purpose with a new subject is para que + subjunctive (pudieran). Porque gives a cause and takes the indicative; por que is not a purpose link.

b1-10.q: Find the mistake: «En Antigua se ve muchas puertas con aldabas de bronce.»
b1-10.why: Puertas is plural, so the se verb must be plural too: se ven. Singular se ve only fits a singular noun or a verb with no noun.

b1-10.q: In which sentence does the future express a guess, not a future event?
options: Si tienes suerte, esta noche verás la lava.
Si caminamos por esa calle, encontraremos la casa.
Si vuelves el año que viene, iré contigo.
b1-10.why: ¿Será alguien…? wonders about the present ('could it be someone…?'). The other sentences talk about real future events.

b1-10.q: What does «Por eso la llamamos Antigua» mean?
options: That's why we call it Antigua.
We call it Antigua for that purpose.
We call it Antigua through that.
b1-10.why: Por eso looks back at a cause: 'that's why'. Para eso would mean 'for that purpose', which isn't what Bayron means.

options: Las alfombras no se hace para durar.
Las alfombras no se hacen por durar.
Las alfombras no se hacen para durar.
Las alfombras no hacen para durar.
b1-10.why: Plural noun, plural se verb (se hacen), and purpose is para + infinitive. Without se, 'the carpets don't make' makes no sense.

acaba: to finish (acabar de + infinitive: to have just done something)
hacerse: to become (hacerse ilusiones: to get one's hopes up)
será: to be (¿será…?: can it be…?, I wonder if…)
